Identity & governance

Companion roles, capability boundaries, and a clear separation between style and authority.

Systems

Separate the roles#

The ABI README describes Abbey as the primary empathetic-polymath profile, Aviva as the direct expert mode, and ABI as the orchestration and governance layer. These descriptions define interaction roles; they do not independently verify separate services or models.

The companion repository is linked by ABI, but its build and deployment were not assessed as part of this preview. Refer to current implementation evidence before assigning any concrete capability to a companion interface.

Style does not grant authority#

A warmer tone, expert mode, or recognizable identity should not be used as evidence that a system has credentials, access to private data, or permission to take external actions. Those properties need explicit configuration and authorization.

As a design principle, interfaces should make proposed actions, scope, and outcomes understandable. This principle is not a claim that a particular backend policy was verified by generating a website.

Keep claims inspectable#

A claims ledger is useful only when a claim can be traced to evidence with a clear scope. An appealing personality is not evidence of consciousness, model quality, autonomy, or a persistent personal memory system.

Use the source identity specification for the project’s current mapping of implemented, partial, and proposed behavior. This page links that reference; it does not certify it.
